newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: WOLTERS KLUWER 1996 PROFIT UP SIX PERCENT.
newsitem.headline: WOLTERS KLUWER 1996 PROFIT UP SIX PERCENT.

text.p: Dutch business publisher Wolters Kluwer NV said on Friday its net profit rose six percent to 479 million guilders from 452 million in 1995, right in line with market expectations.
Sales jumped 47 percent to 4.3 billion guilders, largely as a result of its early 1996 takeover of U.S. tax publisher CCH.
Earnings growth lagged sales growth because the company wrote off 65 million guilders in goodwill from the CCH buy.
But this did not affect cash flow from operations which rose 45 percent to 985 million guilders.
Wolters Kluwer raised its dividend to 2.48 guilders per share from 2.16 guilders and said it was raising its dividend payout ratio to around 35 percent from just over 30 percent.
The company said it expected to return to its customary double-digit earnings growth this year, with earnings per share rising by at least 15 percent per year from 1997 to 1999.
Wolters Kluwer was recently ranked as the third most profitable company in the Financial Times Global 500 which also ranked it as one of the top 10 media companies in terms of market capitalisation.
